fieldMarks: Slender white transverse bars across the back (NatureServe).
Widely separated posterior collars; no black pigment lining the mouth (NatureServe).
Adult males: strongly laterally compressed tail with a white or off-white dorsal stripe, pale patternless head, and enlarged dark inguinal patches (NatureServe).
Up to about 5 in (127 mm) snout-vent length (theNAT).
behavior: Eats arthropods, small lizards and sometimes plant material (NatureServe).
Seasonal activity begins in March-April; members of the genus can lay two clutches a year (NatureServe).
habitat: Rocky areas in arid and semiarid country, usually with scant vegetation: hillsides, alluvial fans, canyons and lava flows (NatureServe).
range: Desert slopes of the Peninsular Ranges in southern California north to the San Jacinto Mountains near Palm Springs, and much of Baja California; an isolated Tecate Mountain (San Diego County) population needs confirmation (NatureServe; theNAT).

lookalikes.name: Great Basin collared lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Great Basin lacks the widely separated posterior collars and slender white dorsal bars (NatureServe); listed as similar species by theNAT.
